content.jointProblem: Can Serbian morphological normalization combined with script-aware token canonicalization or query expansion reduce LinguaBot's retrieval misses while supporting new terminology without a full re-index? The first experiment would compare these alternatives against the current Elasticsearch baseline on held-out support queries, explicitly testing within-word script mixing and banking terminology; reducing the reported 18% miss rate below 5% is a hypothesis, not an assured outcome.

rationale.text: His research directly examines the interaction between Serbian morphological reduction and script normalization, including the order of preprocessing operations.

sources.quote: U ovom radu ispitujemo kako stemovanje i lematizacija interaguju s postupkom normalizacije skripte pri izgradnji pretražnog indeksa.

rationale.text: He has evaluated phoneme-based token canonicalization for Serbian retrieval, providing a concrete candidate method for cross-script matching.

sources.quote: The phoneme-based canonical form reduced the out-of-vocabulary rate from 9.3% to 2.1% compared with a Latin-only baseline

rationale.text: He has studied query-time transliteration expansion, offering an alternative to changes concentrated entirely in the index.

sources.quote: This paper studies the effect of automatically expanding queries with their transliteration variants before submission to an inverted index.

rationale.text: His production-oriented work compares deterministic and neural normalization, including a selective neural fallback that could be tested under LinguaBot's resource limits.

sources.quote: deterministic normalizer with neural fallback triggered only for out-of-vocabulary tokens
reaches MRR of 0.66 with a 99th-percentile latency overhead of only 9 ms.

rationale.text: He has experience integrating script normalization into company search pilots, rather than only evaluating standalone algorithms.

sources.quote: Ovaj rad opisuje iskustva iz tri pilot implementacije interne pretrage zasnovane na open-source pretražnom okviru dopunjenom modulom za normalizaciju pisma

constraints.text: The prototype must address Serbian-specific inflection and mixed-script typos, including within-word mixing, and be evaluated against the existing Elasticsearch setup.

sources.quote: Our current Elasticsearch setup uses a basic stemmer that was built for Croatian and misses a significant share of Serbian-specific forms.
our users freely switch between Latin and Cyrillic script mid-sentence — sometimes mid-word in typos.

constraints.text: Vocabulary updates must work without a full re-index and avoid dependence on continually maintained manual synonym lists.

sources.quote: can be updated when new vocabulary arrives without a full re-index.
maintaining those lists manually does not scale as clients add new product terminology every quarter.

constraints.text: Evaluation must use the available labelled support data and linguistic validation, with the company's below-5% miss-rate goal treated as an acceptance target to test.

sources.quote: We have a labelled query-response dataset of around 85,000 pairs across all clients, and our two in-house linguists can annotate or validate proposed solutions.
A good outcome is getting that 18% miss rate below 5% and keeping it there with a manageable maintenance process.

constraints.text: Scope tooling and data work around EUR 8,000 and deliver a testable prototype within six months; the total research-contract budget still needs clarification.

sources.quote: Budget for tooling or data work is modest — around 8,000 EUR — and we want something testable within six months.

constraints.text: Keep the researcher's contribution to a small industrial contract or consulting engagement, with a substantive research question rather than general software development.

sources.quote: Trenutno je angažovan na dva aktivna projekta, ali ima kapaciteta za jedan manji industrijski ugovor ili konsultantski angažman.
nije zainteresovan za opšte projekte razvoja softvera bez istraživačke komponente.

risks: Published results largely concern legal, news, web or encyclopedia retrieval, not short banking and telecom support queries. Transfer to product terminology and within-word script typos is unvalidated and must be tested in the first experiment.
Canonicalization and morphological reduction may merge distinct terms or mishandle foreign names, abbreviations and alphanumeric product identifiers. Better recall could therefore reduce precision.
Prior company pilots still required terminology updates, and incremental news indexing does not establish that changing normalization rules can avoid re-indexing existing Elasticsearch documents.
The 18% baseline comes from one bank's sample; performance across all clients and the precise definition of a useful result remain unknown.
Elasticsearch-version compatibility, deployment hardware, latency limits, client-data access permissions and hosting restrictions are unknown and could prevent integration or evaluation.
Participation is open, but the researcher's start date and actual time allocation are unknown. His limited capacity and an unspecified research-fee budget could make the six-month scope infeasible.
questions: Can the researcher confirm a start date and time allocation for a small six-month joint project, and who among LinguaBot's engineers will own implementation?
Does EUR 8,000 cover only tooling and data work, or also researcher fees, infrastructure and integration?
Can query logs, relevance labels and corresponding knowledge-base snapshots be shared in an approved environment, and what anonymization, client-consent and data-retention requirements apply?
How is 'no useful result' defined, at what retrieval depth, and should below 5% be demonstrated for each client or across an aggregate held-out set?

Can the linguists create a first-experiment test set stratified by inflection, script switching, within-word mixing, unseen terminology and ambiguous product identifiers, with client- and time-separated evaluation splits?
Which Elasticsearch version, analyzers, plugins, hardware and latency limits apply, and does the no-full-re-index requirement also prohibit an initial migration?
How frequently does terminology change, what update effort is acceptable, and can query-time normalization or expansion satisfy the update requirement without changing stored token representations?
